name: Acute Peripheral Arterial Occlusion

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Imaging Criteria for Acute Peripheral Arterial Occlusion

criteria.description: Sudden onset of limb ischemia symptoms including pain, pallor, pulselessness, paresthesia, paralysis, and poikilothermia
Absent or diminished distal arterial pulses in the affected limb
Confirmation of arterial occlusion by Doppler ultrasound, CT angiography, or conventional angiography
History of embolic events or thrombosis predisposing to arterial occlusion
Coldness of the affected limb compared to contralateral side

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of sudden limb ischemia symptoms with absent distal pulses and imaging confirmation of arterial occlusion
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Early diagnosis is critical to prevent limb loss; clinical suspicion should prompt urgent vascular imaging.

laboratory: Elevated serum lactate in severe ischemia
Increased creatine kinase (CK) in muscle injury
Possible metabolic acidosis in prolonged ischemia
imaging: Doppler ultrasound showing absent or reduced arterial flow
Conventional angiography confirming site and extent of occlusion
other: Physical exam findings of 6 Ps: pain, pallor, pulselessness, paresthesia, paralysis, poikilothermia

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of limb swelling and pain without pulselessness
Venous Doppler shows venous thrombosis rather than arterial occlusion
Gradual onset of claudication rather than sudden ischemia
Presence of collateral circulation and less severe acute symptoms
Neurological symptoms without vascular signs such as pulselessness or pallor

redFlags: Signs of tissue necrosis or gangrene
references: Norgren L, Hiatt WR, Dormandy JA, et al. Inter-Society Consensus for the Management of Peripheral Arterial Disease (TASC II). J Vasc Surg. 2007;45 Suppl S:S5-67.
Creager MA, Kaufman JA, Conte MS. Clinical practice. Acute limb ischemia. N Engl J Med. 2012;366(23):2198-206.
Rooke TW, Hirsch AT, Misra S, et al. 2011 ACCF/AHA Focused Update of the Guideline for the Management of Patients With Peripheral Artery Disease. Circulation. 2011;124(18):2020-45.
